name: Greenish umber

sections.title: Greenish umber is a dark olive-brown carried into our library from the Japanese traditional color Yanagisusutake, "sooty willow bamboo," and it sits 11.7 units from the plain [[umber]].
sections.body:
Our library lists this color under the Japanese name Yanagisusutake, written 柳煤竹, combining *yanagi* (willow), *susu* (soot) and *take* (bamboo) [1]. No book consulted independently dates the coinage beyond that library gloss, so it is undocumented here [1].

The swatch measures lightness 32, chroma 11 and hue 103 degrees, filed under Neutrals and used chiefly for painter's pigments [1]. The nearest named colors on file are [[guinea-hen]], [[dark-olive]], [[dark-olive-grey]] and [[dark-olive-grey]], at 2.6, 3.4, 3.4 and 3.4 ΔE [1]. A lighter, more saturated relative in the same name set is [[grey-celadon]].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: A color within range of this swatch appears in 4,172 of the 23,781 paintings in our archive, about 17.5 percent, as photographed, roughly split evenly between mid-tone and shadow use [2]. The earliest dated match is a 138 CE Egyptian funerary panel, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2]. Arnoud van Halen carries it in 31 of 50 dated paintings, 3.5 times the archive's overall rate[2].
